line: They know my name ring bells so they still press Say the Queen name you can get some ill press
vault_lines: They know my name ring bells so they still press
meaning:
“My name rings bells” is an idiom used to express how popular or familiar a person is. Nicki uses it here as a double entendre though, to ring a door bell, you have to press it. But also because she is so popular, her competition presses her and tries to create conflict.

There is also a play on the homophones “still/steal.” People use Nicki’s name as a way to steal the press' attention from artists more deserving.

By consistently mentioning Nicki’s name, you can get more press in the media, then you normally would.

Although, the use of the word “ill” is intentionally double meaning. While it can mean that the artist mentioning Nicki is getting more press, it can also mean they are getting bad press. This bad press
 is most likely backlash from her fans or possibly Nicki firing back with a verse.

vault_lines: Yo, Lil’ bitch I heard these labels tryna make another me
meaning:
Nicki accuses other labels of trying to imitate her success by scrambling to find the next Nicki Minaj. The way she words it is similiar to how Jay Z made the same point in “Lost One”:

I heard motherfuckers sayin' they made Hov
Made Hov say, “Okay, so, make another Hov!

English rapper, Lady Leshurr, leant credibility to this view by publicly admitted that Atlantic Records offered to sign her if she would start beef with Nicki Minaj, however Leshurr refused this offer.

However Nicki has long been accused of pulling levers behind the scenes to try and prevent the rise of other female rappers. This was a charge levelled at her by Remy Ma, who claimed in an interview that Nicki was trying “stop her bag”. Cardi B has also accused Nicki Minaj of trying to do this.

Nicki flips these claims by pointing out that it’s not her fault that others aren’t successful by referencing Shaggy’s song “It Wasn’t Me”. In 2018 she continued to play on this theme, releasing a branded line of merch with the phrase “Nicki stopped my bag” emblazoned on it.

It was also revealed in 2018 that Nicki believed Cardi B intentionally tried to prevent her (as of 2018) husband Offset and 21 Savage from appearing in the music video for “No Flag”, claiming on her Beats 1 Radio Show that:

Offset and 21 Savage didn’t do that London On Da Track record because she [Cardi] said I was talking about her…It was clear she wanted to turn them against me and that’s what she did

 This lends further credence to these lines also being subs at Cardi.
